cve_summary: epan/dissectors/packet-dcerpc-spoolss.c in the SPOOLS component in Wireshark 1.12.x before 1.12.12 and 2.x before 2.0.4 mishandles unexpected offsets, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (infinite loop) via a crafted packet.
commit_message:
SPOOLSS: Try to avoid an infinite loop.

Use tvb_reported_length_remaining in dissect_spoolss_uint16uni. Make
sure our offset always increments in dissect_spoolss_keybuffer.

Change-Id: I7017c9685bb2fa27161d80a03b8fca4ef630e793

docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Dissects a key buffer from a given packet, extracting its size and data.

Parameters: 
tvb (tvbuff_t *): Pointer to the packet buffer to dissect.
offset (int): The starting position in the buffer for dissection.
pinfo (packet_info *): Information about the packet being dissected.
tree (proto_tree *): The protocol tree to which the dissected data will be added.
di (dcerpc_info *): Information related to the DCERPC protocol.
drep (guint8 *): Pointer to the data representation.

Returns: 
int: The new offset after dissection, or an adjusted offset in case of overflow.

Logic: 
The function first checks if the DCERPC connection is conformant. It then extracts the size of the key buffer and calculates the end offset. If an overflow is detected, it adjusts the end offset to prevent accessing invalid memory. It continues to dissect the key buffer data until the end offset is reached or the offset is invalid.
"""
